pairs.subject: generative-provider-routing
pairs.evidence: lib/sound/batch.ts:65 A batch names a kind (music|sfx) and one chokepoint asks the desk's engine registry whether that engine may make it, so no surface picks the engine; the refusals, unpriced figures and receipts around it also hold.

techniques.evidence: lib/sound/batch.ts:65 One seam maps a capability to an engine and checks it against the registry (`can`). Each capability row has one entry (music->suno, sfx->elevenlabs, line 66), and the file header explains why. One weak spot: generate.ts:136 makes the caller send provider "elevenlabs" and accepts nothing else.
lib/sound/batch.ts:71 When an engine is withheld, the error carries the registry's own reason word for word. It does not collapse into a generic failure.
lib/sound/sfxJob.ts:51 Effects are marked unpriced and say why, instead of carrying an invented price. The plan step carries usd: null plus that reason (line 172).
lib/sound/batch.ts:154 An N-clip batch is priced as N units on one receipt before anything launches. The launch happens only when the receipt's token is confirmed.

lib/sound/sfxJob.ts:186 Only rate limits, timeouts and failures are retried. A MusicError 'refused' is fatal, so the same vendor is never retried on a refusal. Each capability has one vendor, so there is nowhere to hop to.

pairs.subject: generative-provider-routing
pairs.evidence: lib/spend/meter.ts:249 A settled call with no figure books no row and only bumps counters.unpriced. Its hold is deleted in the same settle, so the next `spent + held + amount > ceiling` check treats the unpriced call as free, breaking the 'unreported cost still counts against the next ceiling check' rule.

techniques.evidence: lib/spend/meter.ts:249 The check before the call conforms (line 343). Booking actuals does not: the estimate is not booked when no actual figure arrives, so unpriced counts as zero against the window.

lib/spend/meter.ts:441 The budget is a band: a reporting-only floor that every class declares (classes.ts floorVar), and a breach of it is reported. Whether the plan's top entry was ever called is not tracked here.

packages/kernel/src/spend-requests/schema.ts:84 Each receipt line in a spend request carries its figure's source, plus a nullable usd with an unpricedReason (lines 81-83). An estimate cannot pass as a receipt.

pairs.subject: generative-provider-routing
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/produce/produce.ts:56 The receipt shows the provider and model the router chose, prices N units as N, never draws an unpriced figure as a dollar amount, and tags every figure with its source, so a receipt and an estimate cannot be confused.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/produce/produce.ts:56 An unpriced cost is drawn as 'unpriced' plus a reason chip (Unpriced.tsx), never $0. Receipt.tsx:81 tags each line's figure source.

packages/ui/src/components/produce/produce.ts:65 Fan-out is priced as N units, and the receipt is read before the launch. Caveat: mayStopAtCeiling (line 196) does not count unpriced lines toward the ceiling warning. They are counted separately as a chip.

packages/ui/src/components/produce/Receipt.tsx:3 The surface displays the vendor the router chose and does not choose one itself. The model picker only steers among the server's options, and only while the plan is a draft (PlanTable.tsx:10).
packages/ui/src/components/produce/RerouteList.tsx:8 This is an operator re-route between server-computed options, not a vendor refusal hop. The UI calls no vendor.
